transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. Um, so what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I just... I keep getting up when I really shouldn't. Like, during our sprint planning meetings at work, or even these long mortgage calls I've been having lately. 

We're trying to refinance the house, actually, and the rates are just completely ridiculous right now. My husband spent like three hours on the phone with the broker yesterday, and they keep asking for the exact same tax documents we already uploaded to their portal. It's so frustrating because their website is just terrible—I'm a software developer, so bad UI just drives me completely crazy, you know? Like, just put the upload button where people can actually see it! 

But, um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the calls. So even when I know I absolutely need to stay put and listen to the mortgage guy or my project manager, I just... I'll suddenly decide I desperately need a glass of water right that second, or I'll just get up to check something in the other room. Like yesterday I just walked away from my desk to check on my new plant because I remembered it had a brown leaf. I just keep leaving my seat.
Do you often feel restless or have a hard time staying seated, even when you know you need to?

Yeah, definitely. Like, even if I manage to force myself to stay in the chair and I look totally calm on the outside, inside I just feel this... this intense pressure. Like I absolutely need to move or switch to a different task, or just do something with my hands before I literally crawl out of my skin. 

Actually, speaking of doing things with my hands, I bought this custom mechanical keyboard recently for work. It has these really nice tactile switches—Cherry MX Browns, if you know anything about keyboards? They have this great little bump when you press them, which is just so satisfying when you're coding. My coworker Dave has the blue switches, which are super loud and clicky, and honestly kind of obnoxious on Zoom calls. I actually had to mute him during our standup on Tuesday because he was just hammering away while our scrum master was trying to talk about the Q3 deliverables. Dave is always doing that, though, he never mutes his mic when he's typing. 

Wait, sorry, what was I answering? Oh, right, the restlessness. But yeah, that internal pressure to move is just always there when I'm stuck in my chair.
Do you often find yourself struggling to focus or finish tasks, even when they’re important—like at work or when handling things like the mortgage refinance?

Yeah, it's a huge problem. Like, I’ll sit down with totally good intentions to review a pull request for work, or read through those massive PDF mortgage disclosures. But... well, speaking of pull requests, we have this junior developer on my team, Kevin, and he is just notorious for submitting PRs without running the linter first. It drives me up the wall because it's such an easy fix, right? Like, we really just need to automate it in our CI/CD pipeline. 

I've actually been telling my manager we should migrate to GitHub Actions for our workflows because Jenkins is just so clunky and outdated. My last company used Jenkins and it literally crashed every single time we tried to do a Friday deployment... which, by the way, you should never deploy on a Friday anyway, it's just asking for your weekend to be ruined. 

But anyway, wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, focusing on the important stuff. So yeah, I'll start reading Kevin's code or the mortgage paperwork, and after a few minutes I'll suddenly realize I've just been staring at the exact same section of text. Like, my eyes are on the screen, but my brain is completely gone, just thinking about five totally unrelated things at once instead of actually finishing the task.
Looking back, did you notice these same kinds of struggles with restlessness, staying focused, or finishing tasks when you were a child, like in school or at home?

Yeah, actually. I mean, it's funny you ask that because I was just talking to my mom about this the other day. She was over at our house helping us pack up some of the guest room stuff—because if this refinance goes through, we're finally going to finish the basement and turn it into a proper office for me, which would be amazing. Right now my desk is just shoved in the corner of the guest room, and the lighting in there is awful for video calls. I look like a ghost on Zoom half the time. I even bought one of those ring lights, but it reflects off my glasses in this really weird way, so I end up having to take my glasses off, and then I can barely read the screen. 

Anyway, my mom was looking through this box of old school stuff she brought over, and... oh, right, childhood. So yeah, I definitely had those same issues back then. I remember my teachers in elementary school were always having to move my desk around or remind me to stay in my seat. I was just always popping up for no reason, or blurting out answers before the teacher even called on me. And I'd just completely rush through all my assignments, even when I totally understood the material, just to get them over with so I could do something else.

latest_inference.note: The patient reported symptoms consistent with ADHD, including difficulty staying seated, restlessness, trouble focusing, and issues with task completion. These symptoms were present in childhood and persist into adulthood, aligning with the diagnostic criteria for F90.0 (ADHD, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive type). Other candidates (F41.0, F32.0, F06.81) are less consistent with the longitudinal history and core symptomatology described.

This could suggest ADHD (F90.0), anxiety (F41.0), or depression with psychomotor agitation (F32.0). Early signs of dementia (F06.81) cannot be ruled out without further cognitive assessment.
